forecast.desc: The June–September season ended below normal. After the driest June in over a decade (~40% deficit), strong July–August recovery narrowed the seasonal shortfall to roughly the low teens. The +IOD that emerged late supported the back half; IMD's final performance figures were released September 29.
forecast.inference: The season ended better than the June collapse implied but below normal overall — a genuine recovery story. July's low-pressure systems drove a strong rebound, August held, and an emerging positive IOD supported late-season rainfall, narrowing the seasonal deficit from ~40% at end-June to the low teens by season's end. The +IOD proved the meaningful offset the spring analysis anticipated only as a possibility: it counteracted part of the intensifying El Niño's suppression, much as it did in 1997. The residue is a below-normal but not catastrophic season, with the deficit concentrated in the persistent east/northeast and southern-peninsula laggards rather than the core grain belt.

seasonal.desc: The season swung dramatically: the driest June in over a decade, a strong July–August recovery, and a +IOD-supported close. The El Niño peak arrives after the monsoon, in the autumn–winter window.
seasonal.inference: The season inverted the textbook script and then partly recovered. It suppressed rainfall early (a severe June, contrary to the 'monsoon escapes the peak' thesis), then rebounded strongly in July–August as low-pressure systems formed and a positive IOD emerged. The two opposing drivers — an intensifying, near-record El Niño pushing toward suppression versus a +IOD supporting rainfall — fought to a below-normal but manageable outcome. With the monsoon now ending, the El Niño peak moves fully into the post-monsoon Oct–Dec window, where it bears on the northeast monsoon and rabi reservoir refill rather than the main kharif season.

onset.desc: IMD declared Kerala onset on June 4 — three days later than the June 1 normal, and against pre-season forecasts of an early arrival. Onset stalled at both ends for nearly two weeks.
onset.inference: The late onset (June 4) was the leading edge of the June collapse, but it proved a poor guide to the season: the monsoon recovered sharply in July–August despite the poor start, underscoring that onset timing correlates weakly with the seasonal total. The season's arc — late and dry, then strongly recovering — is a reminder that intraseasonal drivers (low-pressure systems, MJO, IOD) can override the ENSO base case over a monsoon's course.

reservoir.desc: Live storage across major reservoirs vs the 10-year average. The July–August recovery replenished storage substantially after the June drawdown, leaving the buffer comfortably above average heading into the rabi season.
reservoir.inference: The buffer that made this a price story rather than a supply-collapse story ends the season in good shape. The strong July–August rains rebuilt storage well above the ten-year average, easing the June drawdown and supporting rabi-season irrigation. Supply is well buffered; the residual risk is price transmission on the specific crops hit by June's deficit and the uneven regional distribution — pulses and oilseeds — where a below-normal seasonal total still argues for watchfulness on food inflation into the Oct–Dec window as the El Niño peaks.

regional.desc: End-of-season regional picture. Central India and the northwest recovered strongly from the June deficit; east/northeast India and the southern peninsula were the persistent laggards throughout.

rows.note: Below normal both halves; NE monsoon next

regional.inference: The regional picture reorganised over the season. Central India — the core rain-fed belt and the worst-hit region in June (~50% deficit) — swung to a July excess and ended near or above normal, the single biggest positive of the recovery; the northwest similarly rebounded. The persistent laggards are east/northeast India and the southern peninsula, which stayed below normal throughout. For the peninsula the focus now shifts to the Oct–Dec northeast monsoon, which an El Niño typically enhances — a potential offset for the region that lagged most this season.
